questions.question: Why should a liveness endpoint like /health usually NOT check the database?
options: Database queries are not allowed in GET handlers
A database outage would make every instance fail liveness and be restarted, which does not fix the database
Liveness probes time out after 10 milliseconds
Prisma cannot run raw queries such as SELECT 1
questions.explanation: Liveness answers 'is this process alive?'. Dependency checks belong in readiness, which takes the instance out of rotation without restarting it.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of pino-http's JSON logs over morgan's text lines in production?
options: Log platforms can index and filter by fields such as request ID, status or userId
JSON logs are never written to stdout
They automatically remove all personal data
They make requests faster than having no logging at all
questions.explanation: Structured logs are machine-searchable. Redaction still has to be configured, for example with pino's redact option.

questions.question: A Prometheus histogram uses the raw URL (e.g. /api/expenses/1937) as its route label. What is the problem?
options: Raw URLs are less accurate than route patterns for timing
Every distinct ID creates a new time series, so label cardinality grows without bound
questions.explanation: Use the route pattern such as /api/expenses/:id to keep a small, fixed set of label values.

questions.question: How should a request ID middleware behave when an incoming request already has an X-Request-Id header?
options: Always overwrite it with a new UUID and hide the original
Reuse it, attach it to the request's logs and echo it in the response header
Store it in a cookie for the next request
questions.explanation: Reusing an upstream ID lets one request be traced across the load balancer and every service; generate one only when it is missing.
